title: CKA vs CKS: Kubernetes Admin or Security?
subtitle: Which Kubernetes cert comes first, and in what order to take them

pros: The baseline Kubernetes cert expected everywhere: Platform / SRE / DevOps with cluster ownership.
Senior median salary of €72k in France, €88k in Luxembourg (Hays 2026).
Hands-on format (live lab, real terminal) — no multiple choice, you do real k8s work.
The official and de facto prerequisite for the CKS (the Linux Foundation won't register you for the CKS without a valid CKA).
cons: Very technical: etcd, control plane, CNI networking, kubeadm, cluster troubleshooting in 2 hours.
$395 to register, ~80-120 hours of realistic prep if you haven't run a production cluster.
Doesn't cover advanced security topics (Pod Security Standards, runtime security, supply chain) — that's exactly the CKS scope.
certs.bestFor: You're targeting Platform Engineer / SRE / DevOps with cluster responsibility. It is your first k8s cert, full stop.

pros: The only globally recognized Kubernetes security cert — strong differentiation on LinkedIn and on a cyber/cloud résumé.
Covers the whole pipeline: Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicy, fine-grained RBAC, secrets, OPA/Gatekeeper, Falco, image signing (Cosign), SBOM, audit logs.
In high demand at fintechs, banks, and any company going through ISO 27001 / SOC 2 on Kubernetes.
A hands-on lab like the CKA — no cramming, you genuinely harden a cluster.
cons: The CKA is a mandatory prerequisite: you pay at least 2 × $395 to get to the CKS.
A shorter but denser exam (2 hours, ~15-20 tasks mixing ops + security).
The pure Platform Engineer market won't require the CKS — it's a bonus, not a job requirement.
Third-party tools (Falco, Trivy, OPA, Cilium) to learn beyond Kubernetes itself: prep goes beyond the official docs.
certs.bestFor: You already hold the CKA plus 1-2 years of production clusters, and you're moving toward Cloud Security Engineer, Platform Security or cluster DevSecOps.

verdicts.profile: You're new to Kubernetes (never run a production cluster).
verdicts.why: The CKS assumes the entire CKA scope — control plane, CNI networking, advanced kubectl. Without those foundations you'll sink within 30 minutes. And the Linux Foundation won't register you for the CKS without an active CKA anyway.

verdicts.profile: You've held the CKA for 1-2 years and want a cert to raise your rate or salary.
verdicts.why: The CKS is the logical next step: few candidates have it (scarcity = premium), it opens the best-paying banking/fintech/healthcare engagements, and it complements the CKA perfectly without duplicating it.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a generalist Platform Engineer / SRE role.
verdicts.why: The CKA is enough for 90% of Platform/SRE postings. The CKS is an appreciated bonus, but no recruiter turns down a qualified CKA holder for lacking the CKS.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a Cloud Security Engineer / DevSecOps / Security Architect role.
verdicts.why: It's the cert that proves you can harden a real cluster — Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicy, OPA, image signing, runtime detection. A CISSP or Security+ doesn't give you that hands-on k8s credibility.

verdicts.profile: You work at a company going through ISO 27001 or SOC 2 on its k8s workloads.
verdicts.why: ISO/SOC 2 audits require concrete controls: Pod Security Standards, default NetworkPolicy, audit logs enabled, image scanning, managed secrets. The CKS gives you exactly the vocabulary and patterns the auditor expects to see.

verdicts.profile: You want the CKA + CKAD + CKS 'trifecta'.
verdicts.why: The canonical order: CKA → CKAD (1-2 months later, gentle curve) → CKS (3-6 months after that, the final boss). The CKS requires the CKA; the CKAD is a useful detour but not a blocker. Taking the CKS before the CKAD is fine.

verdicts.profile: You're hesitating because your training budget is limited to $395 this year.
verdicts.why: The CKA gets you hired; the CKS gets you a raise once you're hired. And you have no choice: you MUST start with the CKA — it is an administrative and technical prerequisite for the CKS. Save $395 for the CKS in 12-18 months.

tldr: CKA = the cert that gets you hired in Platform/SRE. CKS = the one that raises your rate or seniority once you have the CKA plus 1-2 years of production clusters. You can't take the CKS without the CKA, so the order is fixed. Get the CKA first, then the CKS 12-18 months later if your role shifts toward security.
